However the Armor of the Musashi while being thicker was made up of layers that was markedly inferior to the homogeneous hardened monolithic armor of the Iowa's

The Musashi's 18.1 inch guns that fired a 3200 lb Armor piercing projectile at 2600 feet per second vs the 2800 Armor Piercing projectile at 2700 feet per second of the Iowa. However the design of the super heavy Armor Piercing projectile (APCBC Projectile) while being 20% lighter had the same armor piercing capability as the larger and heavier Japanese projectile. Both guns had the same range on paper, But the effective range of the 18 inch guns on the Musashi was 24000 meters vs almost 39000 meters for the 16 inch guns of the Iowa's.

The difference was due to the FORD MK 1 ballistic data computer that the US Navy used on the Iowa. The US Navy's ballistic data computer could be loaded with the speed and bearing of the Iowa, as well as the speed and bearing of the target, the wind direction and speed was and input, the temperature was an input, the rotational speed of the earth was an input and the speed and bearing of the ocean currents was an input. In all over 25 variables could be computed to provide a firing solution. The ballistic data computer gave the the Iowa a edge in a long range gunnery duel.

The IJNS Musashi would NOT have had the edge in gunnery as well as armor as was shown on paper. Another detracting value of the Musashi's was that the top speed of the Musashi was only 27 knots while the top speed of the Iowa was 33 knots (and could reach 35 knots for a short time) In any fight the top speed of the combatant is a deciding advantage as the superior speed gives the faster ship the decision as to when where and how to engage it's opponent.

So the bottom line is the Armor of the two ships was an equal, but the effectiveness and accuracy of the Main gun battery and the superior speed of the Iowa's gave them an advantage over the IJNS ships.
